concepts.name: Article 19(1)(a): Freedom of Speech and Expression - Scope and Extent
key_dimensions: Positive content: right to know, right to information, freedom of press, commercial speech
Negative content: right to silence, right not to speak (Bijoe Emmanuel case)
Symbolic speech and its protection (flag salutation, armbands, black badges)
Exclusions: defamation, contempt of court, incitement to violence, hate speech

concepts.name: Article 19(2): Reasonable Restrictions on Freedom of Speech
key_dimensions: Eight grounds: sovereignty and integrity, security of state, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to offence
Test of reasonableness: procedural and substantive (Chintaman Rao case)
Distinction between 'public order' vs 'law and order' (Romesh Thappar case)
Prior restraint vs subsequent punishment and judicial approach

concepts.name: Freedom of Press and Media Rights under Article 19(1)(a)
key_dimensions: No separate provision but implicit in freedom of speech (Romesh Thappar, Sakal Papers cases)
Right to publish, circulate, and access information
Restrictions on press: Official Secrets Act, contempt, defamation, censorship
Electronic media regulation and licensing requirements (not absolute right to broadcast)

concepts.name: Article 19(1)(b): Freedom to Assemble Peaceably and Without Arms
key_dimensions: Essential conditions: peaceful and unarmed assembly only
Includes right to hold public meetings, demonstrations, processions, dharnas
Restrictions under Article 19(3): sovereignty and integrity, public order only
Section 144 CrPC and its constitutional validity as reasonable restriction

concepts.name: Article 19(1)(c): Freedom to Form Associations or Unions
key_dimensions: Includes right to form political parties, trade unions, companies, societies
Right to continue association but no right to recognition (Damyanti Naranga case)
Negative aspect: right not to associate (compulsory membership issues)
Restrictions under Article 19(4): sovereignty and integrity, public order, morality

concepts.name: Trade Union Rights and Restrictions under Article 19(1)(c)
key_dimensions: Right to form trade unions but no fundamental right to strike (T.K. Rangarajan case)
Right to collective bargaining as part of freedom of association
Reasonable restrictions: registration requirements, prohibition of certain activities
Conflict between individual rights and union membership (closed shop agreements)

concepts.name: Article 19(1)(d): Freedom to Move Freely Throughout India
key_dimensions: Territorial extent: throughout India only (not outside India)
Includes right to travel, reside temporarily, and passage through any part
Restrictions under Article 19(5): interests of general public or protection of scheduled tribes
Inner Line Permit system and protected areas as valid restrictions

concepts.name: Article 19(1)(e): Freedom to Reside and Settle in Any Part of India
key_dimensions: Distinction between 'move freely' (19(1)(d)) and 'reside and settle' (19(1)(e))
Permanent vs temporary residence rights
Restrictions under Article 19(5): general public interest or protection of scheduled tribes
Special provisions: Article 370 (J&K - now abrogated), Article 371A (Nagaland)

concepts.name: Article 19(1)(g): Freedom to Practice Any Profession or Carry on Any Occupation, Trade or Business
key_dimensions: Includes right to choose any livelihood, profession, trade, or business
Right to carry on business includes right to advertise (Tata Press case)
Does not include right to carry on illegal, immoral, or harmful activities
Distinction between profession (qualification-based) and business/trade

concepts.name: Article 19(6): Reasonable Restrictions on Profession, Occupation, Trade and Business
key_dimensions: Grounds: interests of general public, professional/technical qualifications
State monopoly in trade/business as valid restriction (nationalization)
Licensing requirements and their reasonableness (liquor trade, dangerous trades)
Complete prohibition vs regulation: test of reasonableness (Narendra Kumar case)

concepts.name: Professional Qualifications and Regulatory Framework under Article 19(1)(g)
key_dimensions: State can prescribe professional or technical qualifications (doctors, lawyers, engineers)
Regulatory bodies: Bar Council, Medical Council - their powers and limitations
Balance between right to practice and public interest in qualified professionals
Arbitrary or excessive qualifications as unreasonable restrictions

concepts.name: Doctrine of Reasonable Restrictions: Tests and Judicial Review
key_dimensions: Procedural reasonableness: proper procedure, authority, and manner
Substantive reasonableness: proportionality between restriction and objective
Direct and proximate nexus test between restriction and permissible ground
Judicial review: courts determine reasonableness, not legislature (Chintaman Rao case)

concepts.name: Availability of Article 19 Rights: Citizens Only
key_dimensions: Available only to citizens, not to foreigners or legal persons (with exceptions)
Companies and corporations: can claim 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) only (Bennett Coleman case)
Distinction from Article 21 which is available to all persons
Loss of citizenship and consequent loss of Article 19 rights

concepts.name: Suspension of Article 19 During Emergency
key_dimensions: Automatic suspension during National Emergency under Article 358
No suspension during President's Rule (Article 356) or Financial Emergency
Article 359: President can suspend enforcement of other rights but not Article 19
44th Amendment: Article 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even under Article 359

concepts.name: Internet Shutdowns and Article 19(1)(a)
key_dimensions: Anuradha Bhasin case: internet access as part of freedom of speech
Requirement of proportionality and necessity for internet restrictions
Indefinite suspension as violation of Article 19(1)(a)
Procedural safeguards: publication of orders, periodic review, limited duration

concepts.name: Commercial Speech and Advertising Rights under Article 19(1)(a)
key_dimensions: Commercial speech protected but subject to greater restrictions (Tata Press case)
Right to advertise as part of freedom of speech and right to business
Misleading advertisements and consumer protection as valid restrictions
Tobacco, alcohol advertising bans: constitutional validity and reasonableness

concepts.name: Right to Privacy and Article 19: Intersection and Evolution
key_dimensions: Privacy initially derived from Article 19(1)(a), (d) (Kharak Singh case - dissent)
Puttaswamy case: privacy as intrinsic to Article 19 freedoms
Surveillance, data protection, and freedom of speech/movement
Aadhaar case: balancing privacy with Article 19(1)(g) - right to livelihood

concepts.name: Sedition Law (Section 124A IPC) and Article 19(1)(a)
key_dimensions: Constitutional validity upheld in Kedar Nath case with narrow interpretation
Distinction between criticism of government and incitement to violence/public disorder
Recent debates: colonial legacy, misuse, and calls for reconsideration
Supreme Court's 2022 direction to keep sedition law in abeyance pending review

concepts.name: Bandhs, Hartals and Article 19 Rights
key_dimensions: Right to protest vs right to work and freedom of movement of others
Voluntary vs forced bandhs: constitutional validity (Communist Party case)
Coercive bandhs violate Article 19(1)(d), (g) of non-participants
State's duty to protect rights of citizens during bandhs and strikes

concepts.name: Doctrine of Proportionality in Article 19 Restrictions
key_dimensions: Modern Dental College case: proportionality as part of reasonableness test
Four-fold test: legitimate goal, rational connection, necessity, balancing
Application in cases of internet shutdowns, restrictions on assembly, trade regulations
Shift from 'reasonable restriction' to 'least restrictive alternative' approach
